pr_title: .NET: Prevent generating mono glue in project folder
pr_body:
- Fixes #83128.
- Supersedes #83129.

```
$ cd ~/some/project
$ /Godot/godot/bin/godot.linuxbsd.editor.dev.x86_64.mono --generate-mono-glue .
ERROR: --generate-mono-glue: Cannot generate Mono glue while running a game project. Change current directory or enable --editor.
   at: handle_cmdline_args (modules/mono/editor/bindings_generator.cpp:4977)
$ /Godot/godot/bin/godot.linuxbsd.editor.dev.x86_64.mono --generate-mono-glue . -e
// works
```

issue_context.title: Godot crashes when generating mono glue if PWD is godot project
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

commit hash: d80ce0c52a097c35bb4d441e7a9c0a76e6342ba4

### System information

Pop OS 22.04

### Issue description

I'm putting this issue in for tracking purposes.  I also have a PR incoming with a fix.

When generating glue following these docs: 

https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/contributing/development/compiling/compiling_with_dotnet.html#generate-the-glue

Godot crashes if it is generated while the PWD is a godot project.

Here is the stacktrace:

1. Create a godot project

3. Generate the mono glue

review_comments: Makes me wonder if we should add complementary cases, either a `is_editor_or_project_manager_hint` or a `is_game/running_hint` or something like it, though I'm not sure how often this particular check is used, or the complement

This is something I'd like to refactor one day, `main.cpp` and the whole logic to infer what mode to run based on context is very hacky.

We should change it so there's a lot more _intent_ on what to run (can still be implicit for the user but the code flow needs to be explicit), and then we can store which run mode we're using in an enum instead of these custom bools.
